record.paper_title: Recent Results and Open Problems on the Hydrodynamics of Disordered Asymmetric Exclusion and Zero-Range Processes
record.context_brief: Finer-scale phase-transition behavior in disordered ZRP
record.original_question: Assume the disordered zero-range process is in the phase-transition regime with finite critical density rho^*. The known hydrodynamic theorem implies that when the initial density is everywhere above rho^*, the macroscopic profile stays fixed on the hydrodynamic scale because the flux is constant there. The open problem is to prove rigorous finer-scale results beyond this trivial hydrodynamic picture, specifically to show whether inhomogeneities form and particles concentrate on exceptionally slow sites when the density is in the high-density regime rho > rho^*.

evidence.quote: Problem 2. In the phase transition case, the hydrodynamic theorem reveals only trivial behavior at high density ρ > ρ∗ (the profile does not move, see Theorem 2). It is expected that on a finer space scale one can see inhomogeneities develop, specifically, that the particles concentrate on exceptionally slow sites. No rigorous results exist to decribe these phenomena.

In the phase transition case this theorem has an interesting consequence: Suppose the initial profile satifies u0(x) ≥ ρ∗ everywhere on R. Then since f is constant for this range of densities, it follows that u(x, t) = u0(x) for all t > 0. In other words, the profile does not change on the hydrodynamic scale.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the one-dimensional disordered zero-range process on Z defined as follows. Let {alpha_x : x in Z} be a collection of strictly positive i.i.d. random rates ("environment") with values in some interval [c,1] (c>0), and let g:N -> [0,infty) be a nondecreasing jump function with g(0)=0, g(k)>0 for k>=1, and bounded increments. A configuration eta in N^Z assigns eta(x) particles to site x; a particle leaves site x at rate alpha_x g(eta(x)) and jumps to x+1 (totally asymmetric case). 

For almost every environment, there is a one-parameter family of invariant product measures nu_phi indexed by a fugacity phi in [0, phi_c], with mean density rho(phi) increasing continuously to a (possibly finite) critical density rho^* = lim_{phi -> phi_c} rho(phi). Assume the disorder is such that rho^* < infinity (the "phase-transition regime"), and let f(rho) denote the hydrodynamic flux as a function of density; f is strictly increasing on [0, rho^*] and constant on [rho^*, infinity). 

The known hydrodynamic limit states that under Euler rescaling, the empirical density u(x,t) satisfies the conservation law u_t + f(u)_x = 0 (in the entropy sense). In particular, if the initial macroscopic profile u_0 satisfies u_0(x) >= rho^* for all x in R, then u(x,t) = u_0(x) for all t > 0.

Problem. In this high-density regime rho > rho^*, prove rigorous finer-scale (sub-hydrodynamic) results describing the microscopic behavior. Specifically, show that as t -> infinity (with appropriate space-time rescaling finer than the hydrodynamic scale), spatial inhomogeneities develop and the excess particle mass concentrates on the sites x of exceptionally small rate alpha_x, and quantify the rate and spatial distribution of this concentration phenomenon.
artifact.status_search_result: Subsequent rigorous work has established condensation on slow sites in several related disordered/inhomogeneous zero-range models (e.g., stationary measures concentrate excess mass on the site(s) of smallest rate, and hydrodynamic limits with Dirichlet conditions at macroscopic defects have been derived). However, a complete rigorous finer-scale description of the inhomogeneity formation and dynamical condensation on exceptionally slow sites for the genuinely disordered (i.i.d. environment) totally asymmetric zero-range process in the supercritical regime rho > rho^* does not appear fully resolved; partial results exist on stationary condensation and on simpler defect-site geometries.

status_evidence.title: Condensation, boundary conditions, and effects of slow sites in zero-range systems
status_evidence.snippet: Hydrodynamic limits and boundary behaviors at macroscopic defect sites in zero-range systems; Dirichlet boundary conditions arise at critical/super-critical slow sites.
status_evidence.claim: Rigorous results on slow-site effects and condensation at defects in ZRP exist, addressing aspects of the finer-scale picture.

status_evidence.title: Condensation in the Zero Range Process: Stationary and Dynamical Properties
status_evidence.snippet: Above the critical density, excess particles condense onto a single site; stationary and dynamical properties studied.
status_evidence.claim: Condensation phenomena above rho^* are established (non-rigorously and in special cases rigorously) at the stationary level.

status_evidence.title: Condensation in zero-range processes with a fast rate
status_evidence.snippet: Recent rigorous analysis of condensation transitions in ZRP with inhomogeneous rates.
status_evidence.claim: Continued partial progress on rigorous condensation results in inhomogeneous ZRP.
